# TerraScale documentation

> TerraScale hosts SQL databases with active-active multi-region writes. A database lives in a set of
> regions, at least one, and every region of the set is an equal peer that commits reads and writes locally.
> There is no home region and committed writes are never reverted. TerraScale-Consistency: fast (default)
> commits in the called region and replicates to the others; strong runs a serializable transaction agreed
> by two of three regions (also BEGIN STRONG or BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE; automatic for DDL and
> secondary UNIQUE writes). Send the newest TerraScale-Bookmark response header back on later requests to read
> your own writes in any region; the SDKs do this automatically.
> Exchange a dashboard API key for a short-lived access token
> at https://auth.terrascale.tech/terrascale/oauth/token (client credentials
> grant), then reach the database three ways:
>
> - HTTP: POST https://api.terrascale.tech/v1/projects/{project}/databases/{database}/sql/execute
>   with {"statements":[{"sql","args","named"}]}. One request is one
>   transaction of 1 to 256 statements, all or nothing.
> - WebSocket: GET .../databases/{database}/sql/ws, subprotocol
>   terrascale.sql.v2, for interactive transactions of at most 5 seconds.
> - Postgres wire: postgresql://{database}@pg.terrascale.tech:5432/{database}
>   with the API key as the password. Postgres syntax, pg_catalog, COPY and LISTEN work.

> Live shapes support where filters and selected columns. End-user tokens read under database rules.
> Agent databases support TTL, forks and database-scoped keys. Point-in-time recovery creates a new database;
> in-place restore is coming. Database deletion destroys backup data keys; physical cleanup is separate.
> Plans enforce write caps and SQL read fair use. Customer-set hard dollar spending caps are coming.
> Copies in the other regions of a database's set are not billed separately. No production replication-lag guarantee is published.
